what: In the TUI, make 1/2/3 select a priority floor (HIGH, MEDIUM+, LOW+) with 'a' equal to 3, keep 0 as the unprioritized-only view in one priority key row, and persist the view (priority, unread/all, archived, upvoted, sort, source type, kind) to $XDG_STATE_HOME/prismis/tui-view.json across launches.
why: Design: docs/work/tui-filter-model/design.md. Reading cascades from HIGH down but 2 and 3 show one priority only, and every launch resets the view the operator built (gh #36, #33); #52's remaining question, what 0 means, is settled by usage on cerebro (6 of 24 upvotes are rescues from the unprioritized view).

criteria.given: items of priority high, medium, low and none
criteria.when: applyFiltersClientSide runs with the priority state set by each of the keys 1, 2, 3, a and 0
criteria.then: it fails if any key shows an item below its floor, hides one at or above it, or if 0 shows anything but the unprioritized items; otherwise 1 shows high, 2 high and medium, 3 and a high, medium and low, and 0 only the none items, and the test is shown red against equality comparison

it fails if the floors read anything but 'Priority: HIGH', 'Priority: MEDIUM+' and 'Priority: LOW+', or 0 anything but 'Priority: UNPRIORITIZED'; otherwise they do, and the help modal lists 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 in one priority row

criteria.given: a model whose seven view fields are each changed from their defaults
criteria.when: a key handled by Update changes the view and a new model is then built from the same XDG_STATE_HOME
criteria.then: it fails if any of the seven fields differs between the two models or tui-view.json was not written; otherwise the new model starts with the saved view, and after R the saved file holds the defaults

criteria.given: an XDG_STATE_HOME with no tui-view.json, one whose file is not valid JSON, and one whose file holds an unknown priority value and a kind absent from the data
criteria.when: a model is built in each and its kinds load
criteria.then: it fails if the missing file produces a status message, if the corrupt file is not named in a status message, or if the unknown values are kept; otherwise all three start with defaults for the bad or missing fields and only the corrupt one reports
it fails if tui-view.json is ever opened for writing in place; otherwise it is written through a temporary file in the same directory and renamed over
it fails on any failing check; otherwise its last line is `verify: PASS`

outOfScope: MEDIUM-only and LOW-only views go away: 2 and 3 now include everything above them, as gh #36 asks.
stakes: Under 1, 2 and 3, the visible items are exactly those at or above the floor, for items of every priority including none, in local and remote mode alike.
The header reads HIGH, MEDIUM+ or LOW+ for the three floors, and 'a' selects the same items as 3.
0 still shows only unprioritized items, and the help modal shows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 as one priority row.
Changing any of the seven view fields and relaunching restores them; R restores and persists the defaults.

A missing view file gives the defaults with no message; an unreadable or corrupt one gives the defaults and a status message naming it; an unknown field value falls back per field; a vanished kind falls back to all.
The view file is written only through a temporary file and rename, at $XDG_STATE_HOME/prismis/tui-view.json or its default.
